[BugFix][Model] Isolate DeepSeek V4.1 on vLLM 0.29 (#17116)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Follow-up to #16925.

vLLM v0.29 does not contain the upstream DeepSeek V4.1 config/model
modules consumed by the new Ascend implementation. Importing the generic
model runner or speculative decoding path on that release can therefore
fail before any model is loaded.

on vLLM 0.29;
- lazily imports the V4.1 attention/cache and hidden-state drafter types
outside the v0.29 release lane;
- skips only the V4.1-specific unit-test cases that require unavailable
upstream modules, while retaining structural and non-V4.1 coverage;
- adds registration coverage proving existing DeepSeek V4/DSpark
registrations remain available on v0.29 and V4.1 remains registered on
newer vLLM versions.

Yes. On vLLM v0.29, DeepSeek V4.1 is intentionally not registered or
imported, so other supported models and nightly tests are not affected
by unavailable upstream V4.1 modules. DeepSeek V4.1 behavior on newer
vLLM versions is unchanged.

- `pre-commit` targeted checks: `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`,
`codespell`, `typos`
- `python -m compileall` for all changed Python files
- `git diff --check`
- static scan of v0.29-missing upstream DeepSeek V4.1 imports and
generic runtime entry points

[BugFix][Attention][MRV2] Avoid RoPE buffer overwrites during DSA prefill (#16929)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Short prefills can be classified as decodes in DSA. With PCP, global and
local metadata then reuse the same RoPE buffer despite having different
positions, so local metadata construction overwrites the global cos/sin
values before they are consumed.

Use the existing `is_prefilling` metadata to avoid shared RoPE buffers
for batches containing actual prefills, while preserving the attention
decode/prefill classification. Extend the short-request regression test
to cover prefill flags and verify that independently allocated RoPE
values survive subsequent buffer writes.

Fixes incorrect output caused by RoPE buffer overwrites during short
prefills with PCP. No API or configuration changes.

The original short-prefill regression is fixed: the France-capital
prompt returned Paris with identical 128-token outputs across 100 runs.

72.73%**. No request failures; two truncated/unparsed answers per run

commits.message:
[Ops][BugFix] Remove duplicate CMake configuration for custom kernels (#11102)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #11099.

`cmake_build_ext.configure()` previously invoked CMake twice in the same
`self.build_temp` directory.

The first invocation already built a complete configure command:

```python
cmake_args += [source_dir]
subprocess.check_call(cmake_args, cwd=self.build_temp)
```

Immediately afterwards, the method invoked CMake again:

```python
subprocess.check_call(
    ["cmake", ext.cmake_lists_dir, *build_tool, *cmake_args],
    cwd=self.build_temp,
)
```

Because `cmake_args` already starts with `"cmake"` and ends with the
source directory, the second invocation expanded approximately to:

```text
cmake <source directory> cmake <configure options> <source directory>
```

CMake warns that the extra `cmake` path is ignored and performs
configuration again. This PR therefore:

- keeps a single CMake configure invocation;
- uses `ext.cmake_lists_dir` as that invocation's source directory,
preserving the per-extension contract;
- removes the redundant second invocation and the now-unused
`build_tool` and `source_dir` variables.

The resulting command has the expected shape:

```text
cmake <configure options> <extension CMake source directory>
```

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No runtime user-facing change. This removes duplicate build setup work
and preserves each extension's declared CMake source directory.

### How was this patch tested?

- `python -m py_compile setup.py`
- `pre-commit run ruff-check --files setup.py`
- `pre-commit run ruff-format --files setup.py`
- `git diff --check`
- Structural check confirming `configure()` has one CMake invocation
using `ext.cmake_lists_dir`
- GitHub Actions on `a0c6679e4`: `pre-commit`, CPU unit tests, and DCO
passed
([run](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/34969724077)).

CI is not fully green yet: `ci-gate` requires a maintainer to add a
test-enabling label because `setup.py` matches the source-code filter.
With no such label, `select-tests` and downstream tests were skipped.
Please add `ready-precise` to trigger selected tests; no workflow bypass
is included in this PR.

Full custom kernel compilation was not run locally because this
environment does not provide the required Ascend build
toolchain/hardware.

commits.message: [BugFix][Model] DeepSeek-V4 Vision: skip vision SWA index build for text-only batches (#16200) ### What this PR does / why we need it? For `is_mm_prefix_lm` models (DeepSeek-V4 vision), the metadata builder in `NPUModelRunner` unconditionally inserts an entry into `mm_req_doc_ranges` for every scheduled request — text-only requests get an empty list. A dict of empty lists is truthy, so the gate if has_prefill and max_image_tokens > 0 and mm_ranges: in the DSA metadata builder passes, and `build_vision_bidirectional_swa_indices` runs on every text-only prefill even though there are no image spans to apply. Profiling shows this costs ~1.1 ms per step (multiple torch kernel launches) on pure-text traffic. Fix: only insert entries for requests that actually carry image spans. A text-only batch now yields an empty dict, so the gate short-circuits and the vision SWA index build is skipped. Mixed batches are unchanged: `build_vision_bidirectional_swa_indices` iterates `mm_prefix_ranges.items()` and empty range lists contributed nothing, so dropping them is semantically a no-op. Related roadmap: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/15462. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No. Text-only batches now skip an unnecessary computation; indices for image-bearing requests are identical. ### How was this patch tested? [Feature][Model] Support pipeline parallelism for GLM-5.3-Flash (#17047)

Implement the PP contract for the Glm5Next architecture on Ascend:

- Propagate the deferred mHC state (post/comb, FP32) together with
hidden_states/residual across PP boundaries so the receiving rank's
first layer continues with hc_post_pre, identical to single-stage
execution (previously the state was dropped and the receiver fell back
to a standalone hc_pre approximation).
- Implement make_empty_intermediate_tensors matching the real mHC
payload (2D hidden_states, 3D residual (B,n,H), post (B,n,1) and comb
(B,n,n) in FP32) so PP ranks > 0 can profile and capture aclgraphs with
the correct shapes; expose it on both the causal LM and the multimodal
wrapper.
- Fail fast when SP-MoE is combined with PP: sp_shard is not idempotent
and would re-shard activations at the rank boundary.
- Add tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_pp.py pinning the payload key set
and the deferred-state hand-off between two stages.

### What this PR does / why we need it?
Implements the pipeline-parallel (PP) contract for the Glm5Next
architecture (GLM-5.3-Flash) so `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1` works on
Ascend.

Previously PP was effectively gated off for this model:

- `Glm5NextForCausalLM` declared `SupportsPP` but never implemented
`make_empty_intermediate_tensors`, so PP ranks > 0 failed at runtime.
- The deferred mHC state (`post` / `comb`) was dropped at stage
boundaries, making multi-stage execution mathematically different from
single-stage execution even if the shape issue had been fixed.

Changes in `vllm_ascend/models/glm5next/model.py`:

1. `Glm5NextModel.make_empty_intermediate_tensors`: placeholder tensors
mirror the real inter-stage payload. With mHC: `hidden_states` (B, H)
2D, `residual` (B, n, H) 3D, `post` (B, n, 1) and `comb` (B, n, n) in
FP32 (matching the hc_pre kernel outputs); non-mHC configs fall back to
plain `hidden_states` / `residual`.
2. `Glm5NextModel.forward`: non-first ranks consume the incoming `post`
/ `comb` so their first layer continues with `hc_post_pre` — identical
to the single-stage math instead of the previous standalone-`hc_pre`
approximation. Non-last ranks ship the full four-tensor state to the
next stage.
3. `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` expose
the factory (the vision tower only executes on the first PP rank).
4. Fail fast when SP-MoE (`use_sequence_parallel_moe`) is combined with
PP: `sp_shard` is not idempotent and would re-shard already-sharded
activations at the rank boundary.

KDA/Mamba state caches, MLA/indexer/tail cache groups, `make_layers`
partitioning and weight loading were verified to be PP-ready unchanged.
### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
- `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1` now works for `Glm5NextForCausalLM` /
`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (previously a runtime error on PP
ranks > 0).
- Combining sequence-parallel MoE with pipeline parallelism now raises
`NotImplementedError` with a clear message (previously silently
incorrect).
### How was this patch tested?
All NPU tests ran against vLLM main @ 84030bbe3d (the verified commit)
with GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 on 8x Ascend 910B.

- **Unit tests**: added `tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_pp.py` (6 tests:
payload key-set parity with the placeholder factory, deferred mHC state
hand-off at both stage boundaries, non-mHC fallback). Full glm5next UT
suite: 99 passed.

- **Greedy cross-PP probe (single-request curl)**: 10 fixed prompts
(EN/ZH/code/math), `temperature=0`, `/v1/completions`, comparing
`DP1xTP8xPP1` vs `DP1xTP4xPP2` vs `DP1xTP2xPP4`. All outputs fluent and
semantically correct; divergences between different TP/PP decompositions
are greedy-drift only (long identical prefixes followed by a fork, e.g.
first difference at char 723 of a 1042-char completion), with no
corruption or degeneration. Example: the "17 sheep, all but 9 die"
riddle is answered correctly (9) by every configuration.

- **AIME2026 accuracy (ais_bench)**: `aime2026_gen_0_shot_chat_prompt`
(30 problems), temperature=1, top_p=0.95, top_k=2, reasoning_effort=max,
max_out_len=128000, batch_size=32, served as TP4xPP2 with
FULL_DECODE_ONLY aclgraph and 131k context: **96.67**, within the
TP-only reference of 93.33 obtained
  with identical generation parameters.

[BugFix] Prefer selected CANN headers over torch_npu ACL snapshot (#17060)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The CANN feature probes use `${ASCEND_HOME_PATH}/include`, but the
native extension previously searched `${TORCH_NPU_PATH}/include` first.
Some torch_npu wheels expose an older ACL header snapshot there, so
CMake could detect `aclrtGetPhyDevIdByUserDevId` in CANN and then fail
to compile the extension because the stale wheel header won the include
search.

This change places the selected CANN toolkit headers before torch_npu's
bundled headers, keeping feature detection and the extension build
consistent.

Fixes #17059

wheel exposes its bundled ACL snapshot from the top-level include path.

[BugFix][Hybrid Mamba] Restore hybrid MTP prefix caching for PD and kv_both pooling (#16449)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Hybrid FullAttention + Mamba models can lose reusable prefix-cache pages
when MTP/EAGLE is on. On a pure PD prefill producer, EAGLE drops a
verified prompt block and the scheduler backs off one whole Mamba
alignment page; with a 1536-token page, repeated prompts report **0
local prefix-cache hits**.

This PR removes the loss without any launch-argument change:

1. Tag pure-producer role onto `KVCacheConfig`; on pure producers skip
the EAGLE last-block drop in both hybrid lookup entry points.
2. Wrap `_mamba_block_aligned_split` to temporarily clear every
supported drop flag (`use_eagle` / `use_eagle_block_drop`), keep the
wrapper outermost, and restore every value in `finally`. If neither
attribute exists (vLLM 0.28.x and newer variants), call through
unchanged.
3. Restrict the EAGLE-group fallback to FullAttention groups — Mamba/GDN
groups contain no draft-model layers.
4. Keep the verifier window on a KV consumer only after a local or
external prefix was actually computed, so a cold `kv_both` prefill still
publishes reusable state; use the same Triton GDN chunk path for cold
prefill and cached-state resume when prefix caching is enabled.

The exemption deliberately does not apply to `kv_both`, which also
decodes and keeps the upstream EAGLE safety drop.

Refs #12781, #13903, #15408, #15592, #16329.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: hybrid MTP deployments with prefix caching now retain reusable
prompt state on pure PD producers and on cold pooled `kv_both` prefills.
No API, config, or launch-command change.

### How was this patch tested?

mean over requests 2..160.

[CI] Restore public package sources after image build (#16843)

## Summary

CI builds pass internal mirrors (`cache-service...svc.cluster.local`) as
`--build-arg`, which were then **persisted into the image** via:

- `pip config set global.index-url` / `trusted-host`
- `sed` on `/etc/apt/sources.list` (Ubuntu) / `/etc/yum.repos.d/*.repo`
(openEuler)
- `ENV RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER` / `RUSTUP_UPDATE_ROOT`
- `~/.cargo/config.toml` (crates.io mirror + git-fetch-with-cli)
- `git config --global url.<proxy>.insteadOf`

As a result, images published to north-12 and synced to quay.io can only
install packages from the unreachable internal mirrors (apt/pip all fail
for external users).

## Changes

Restore public sources after the build so published images remain usable
externally:

1. **apt/yum**: back up `sources.list` / `yum.repos.d` before swapping
in the mirror, restore after installing system packages.
2. **rustup**: drop the `ENV`, pass
`RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER`/`RUSTUP_UPDATE_ROOT` via `RUN`-local `export` so
they are not baked into the image.
3. **cargo/git**: remove `~/.cargo/config.toml` and `git config --global
--unset-all url.<proxy>.insteadOf` after `build_rust.sh`.
4. **pip**: reset `global.index-url` to a public mirror (tuna) and unset
`trusted-host` at the end.

## Test

- [ ] Docker build (default args) still uses public mirrors
- [ ] CI build (internal mirrors) produces an image whose
`pip`/`apt`/`yum` point to public mirrors

- `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.310p`, `Dockerfile.a3`, `Dockerfile.a5`
- `Dockerfile.310p.openEuler`, `Dockerfile.a3.openEuler`,
`Dockerfile.a5.openEuler`, `Dockerfile.openEuler`

[Feature][Spec Decode] Support GLM-Next MTP with split KV cache groups (#16793)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR fixes GLM-Next MTP speculative decoding when the drafting layers
use multiple physical KV cache groups with different storage layouts.

Previously, draft attention metadata was built under the assumption that
all drafting layers shared the same physical KV cache group. For
GLM-Next, the SFA attention cache and `indexer.k_cache` may belong to
different physical groups and use different storage block sizes. Reusing
the primary group's block table and slot mapping for every layer could
therefore address the wrong cache location.

This PR:

- Builds an independent `AttentionGroup` for each physical KV cache
group used by the drafting layers.
- Preserves each group's own KV cache specification, block table,
storage block size, and slot mapping.
- Advances shared MTP state—such as sequence lengths and
positions—exactly once per speculative step.
- Derives per-group attention metadata from the same updated logical MTP
step, avoiding repeated sequence-state updates.
- Keeps `indexer.k_cache` mapped with its logical scheduler block size
while using its own physical storage layout.
- Reserves request-owned KPool tail capacity for both committed tokens
and speculative lookahead tokens.
- Allows rejected speculative tokens to be rolled back without
overwriting the request's committed KPool tail state.
- Adds unit and Triton operator coverage for the new KPool tail capacity
and rollback behavior.
- Updates the KPool tail compression documentation.

Without this change, GLM-Next MTP can use incorrect cache addresses or
corrupt KPool tail state when speculative tokens are rejected.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, this changes runtime behavior for GLM-Next models using MTP
speculative decoding with split KV cache groups.

There is no public API or configuration change. The user-visible effect
is that this configuration can run correctly with group-specific KV
cache layouts, and rejected speculative tokens no longer corrupt the
committed KPool tail state.

Non-MTP speculative decoding paths retain their existing metadata-update
behavior.

flag, or weight-retention workaround is introduced.

failing [nightly

release on supported hardware, the first call frees the source

startup fails before performance testing; the later ready=2/6 timeout is
a symptom. DFlash and TP4 are not established prerequisites.

[BugFix][SpecDecode] Skip over-limit drafting with DP alignment (#16512)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

A target-model step can fit while the following speculative drafter
query would exceed the drafter's effective `max_model_len`. This PR
aligns Ascend with the batch-level control flow merged upstream in vLLM
[#40589](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40589), and applies
it consistently to every speculative method.

- Check `max_seq_len + drafter_query_width` once on the host before
entering the proposer.
- Reserve the standard `K` draft queries, `K + 1` for DFlash, and
`AscendDSparkProposer.num_query_per_req` for DSpark's exact
anchor/non-anchor query group.
- When the query does not fit, publish empty drafts so stale tokens or
probabilities cannot escape from the previous step.
- For model-backed proposers with DP > 1, keep collective order aligned
with ranks that still draft: DSpark runs one complete synthetic query
group; the other model-backed proposers use the upstream one-token dummy
path.
- N-gram/suffix and other non-model proposers do not run an unnecessary
model dummy. DP = 1 skips the dummy as well.
- Only the last PP rank owns the drafter. Non-owning PP ranks neither
apply a local drafter limit nor join drafter DP work, which avoids PP/DP
divergence when `broadcast_pp_output` is enabled.

The ordinary short-sequence path adds only host integer/method checks.
It adds no NPU operation, collective, request mask, or kernel branch.

This is a new alternative to #16502 and #16153; those earlier PRs and
branches remain unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. If the complete speculative query would exceed the effective
drafter length, that local batch step falls back to target-only
decoding. Target decoding continues normally, and model-backed multi-DP
ranks preserve their drafter collective sequence through the aligned
dummy invocation.

This specifically covers the `current input length + speculative query
width > effective drafter max_model_len` boundary. The target model's
own length limit remains scheduler-owned.
